summary:
OUTPOST SELENE is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar and Martian outpost survival simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge.

Players command a four-person outpost on the Moon or Mars, walk across curved planetary terrain, manage life-support and power systems, grow food, assign crew, launch rover expeditions and respond to environmental hazards. The experience also features an interactive astronomical sky: users can advance mission time, observe changing planetary positions, track and zoom in on celestial bodies, and view calculated local sunrise and sunset information.

Players balance electricity, battery storage, oxygen, water, food and crew safety while completing mission objectives across three difficulty levels. NASA and JPL scientific references inform the educational sky and mission context, while simplified models make complex systems understandable.

By combining free surface exploration, time-dependent planetary visualization and consequential engineering decisions, OUTPOST SELENE turns space science into hands-on STEM learning and builds systems thinking, resource planning, problem-solving and scientific curiosity.
details:
OUTPOST SELENE is an interactive 3D space-survival and mission-management simulation developed using JavaScript, Three.js and Vite.

Players can choose between the Moon and Mars, select mission duration and difficulty, and command a four-person outpost. The game features an immersive 3D planetary environment with curved lunar and Martian surfaces, realistic-looking terrain details, interactive camera controls and free surface movement. Players can walk around the outpost using keyboard controls or an on-screen direction pad.

One of the project's key innovations is its interactive astronomical sky simulation. It uses approximate JPL planetary position models and IAU body-rotation models to calculate celestial positions as mission time advances. Players can observe the Sun, planets and natural satellites, track individual celestial bodies, zoom in on them, and inspect their altitude, azimuth and visibility above or below the local horizon. The system also calculates local sunrise and sunset information. Mars follows its approximately 24.66-hour solar day, while the Moon follows its approximately 29.53-day visual solar cycle.

The mission-management system includes solar array deployment, electricity generation, battery storage, oxygen generation, water recycling, greenhouse cultivation, food harvesting, crew assignments, rover exploration, scientific sample collection and research activities. Players must also respond to dust events, radiation hazards, equipment problems and changing resource conditions.

The game includes three difficulty levels, an interactive tutorial, mission objectives, weather forecasts, crew monitoring, an event log, a field guide and mission debriefing.

The project draws on NASA and JPL scientific references, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter illumination research, Curiosity's Radiation Assessment Detector, NASA Veggie, life-support engineering references, planetary position models and celestial rotation data. These are used to inform simplified educational simulations rather than live NASA data feeds.

OUTPOST SELENE makes space science more engaging by combining planetary exploration, astronomical visualization and practical engineering decisions. It aims to develop scientific curiosity, systems thinking, critical problem-solving and resource-management skills among students aged 8–18+.
